lots.guide_summary: All surviving evidence is SOLD: six Gowans hammers for close gold-framed shell cameo brooches, $120 to $330 (Oct 2025 to Oct 2026), plus one old US sale of a 14k cameo brooch/pendant at about A$143 (2023, not used for bids). No unsold or asking evidence survives. Most comps are portrait cameos, which usually sell better than florals, so this lot should sit in the lower half. An antique 'inscribed 1875' 9ct cameo made $840 (lot 414442, June 2026) but is an outlier and not comparable.
lots.working: Keep: lowest surviving close SOLD in 24 months = $120 (lot 441739, Oct 2026). 120 / 1.198 = 100.2, round down to $100 hammer ($119.80 all-in). Flip: likely resale about $200 (Gowans close comps median about $235, discounted for a floral subject), less about 15% selling fees ($30) and $10 postage = $160. 160 / 2.396 = 66.8, round down to $65. Rate for Simpson: 1.4328 AUD per USD. No melt figure as weight is not stated.
lots.confidence_reason: K14 stamp read in the photos and six Gowans SOLD records checked (API JSON plus their photos), but all are close, not identical (portrait, mostly 9ct, sizes and weights unknown), the K14 mark is unverified by testing, and the weight is unknown.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped: (1) lot 375043 '9CT GOLD LINED FRENCH CAMEO PENDANT': the API shows $26 hammer (2600 cents), not the $90 the researcher claimed, and 'gold lined' is not solid gold. (2) lot 428916 '9CT GOLD CAMEO PENDANT ON CHAIN' $90: photo shows a tiny cameo pendant on a chain, not comparable to a large brooch/pendant. (3) lot 441758 'CAMEO BAR BROOCH & ASST PENDANTS ETC' $40: mixed lot, not a gold cameo. Moved: Simpson Galleries from ASKING to SOLD (page opened, Sold $100.00), kept out of bid working as it is over 24 months old.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3 clearly shows a K14 stamp in a cartouche on the back rim; the Gowans title 'unmarked 9ct' is wrong. Floral shell cameo (large rose with two smaller blooms and leaves), crisp carving, no cracks or repairs visible on the front at enlargement. Six claws, fold-down bail and a long brooch pin that looks gold-coloured (unmarked as far as seen). Shell back is smooth with no visible cracks. Frame shows light surface wear.
lots.condition: Appears good: carving crisp, no visible cracks or chips, frame lightly worn. Pin and bail metal unconfirmed.
lots.question_for_gowans: The frame is stamped K14 but the title says unmarked 9ct: can you confirm the mark and test it? What is the total weight and the size in mm? Are the pin and bail gold or base metal, and is there any crack in the shell when held to the light?
